title: Actions policy lives in one file; its line-1 regal directive also ignores file-length
answers: why does regal report file-length on policy.rego
where should a new GitHub Actions policy rule go
regal ignore file-length directive for the Actions policy file
why is all workflow policy in a single rego file
body:
Convention: all GitHub Actions policy rules live in the single file .github/policy.rego; do not split them into per-rule rego files.
The file's line-1 directive `# regal ignore:directory-package-mismatch,file-length` suppresses regal's file-length limit, because the file sits near that limit and any non-trivial addition trips it.
Adding a rule means adding a deny_* set rule in .github/policy.rego and keeping the directive on line 1; removing the file-length entry will make regal lint fail on the next addition.
Constraints: the directive is the reviewed fix from this change; the one-file layout is described as deliberate in the PR, not enforced by a check.
Applies: Editing .github/policy.rego and its regal lint configuration.
applies: Changes to .github/policy.rego; does not apply to other rego files or to workflow YAML.
says: Continuous integration fails because workflow policy document exceeds maximum allowed length
Pull request linter check fails when adding new automation workflow security rules
Keep all workflow automation compliance rules inside a single central policy definition
Ignore policy length limits so automated pipeline validation checks do not fail

search: All GitHub Actions policy rules must be placed in .github/policy.rego as deny_* set rules rather than split into per-rule files. The line-1 directive `# regal ignore:directory-package-mismatch,file-length` suppresses regal's file-length limit and must be retained when adding rules. This convention applies to .github/policy.rego and its regal lint configuration, not to workflow YAML or other rego files.
